title: Base change of the explicit product-graph compositor
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring. For arbitrary schemes X,Y,Z,X',Y',Z', let f:X→Y, g:Y→Z, f':X'→Y', g':Y'→Z', a:X'→X, b:Y'→Y, c:Z'→Z form Cartesian squares (a,f',f,b), (b,g',g,c), and (a,g'f',gf,c). Supply compactifications of f,g,gf,f',g',g'f' [lem-etale-unbounded-compact-support-composition], and assume only f',g',g'f' quasi-compact. Work in the ordinary unbounded etale A-module derived categories. Write F_v for the compact-support functor of the supplied compactification, L_v for left-derived inverse image, and Ex_v for rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap of the supplied square. Let E:F_gf≅F_f⋙F_g and E':F_g'f'≅F_f'⋙F_g' be exactly sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso on those compactifications. Then for every M, L_c(E_M);Ex_g(F_f M);F_g'(Ex_f(M)) = Ex_gf(M);E'_(L_a M). Canonical functor associators are understood. No quasi-compactness of f,g,gf, Noetherianity, boundedness or constructibility is assumed. Input comparisons and their normalizations are [lem-r9-exact-exchange-pasting], [lem-pur-etale-graph-comparison-base-change], [lem-pur-etale-graph-comparison-interchange], and [lem-pur-etale-proper-open-exchange-cube].

source.place: Tags 0F7F and 0F7J; explicit normalization and factor pasting in lem-route-exists-right-derived-lower-shriek-comp-iso

proof.text: Build the proper product graph diagram and identify its normalized diagram compositor with sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso. Use graph shrinking comparison, the graph cocycle, Cartesian normalization of the proper/open interchange and naturality.

Pull back the diagram factor by factor using fibre-product universal properties. Apply proper and open exact exchange pasting and the arbitrary-base-change proper/open cube. Paste these identities, moving factors by naturality.

Use the graph comparison base-change theorem and the open presentation normalization at both endpoints. Its quasi-compact refinement normalization identifies the pulled-back compactification comparisons with the prescribed common-refinement isomorphisms.

Compare the pulled graph diagram and the primed chosen graph diagram by graph/interchange compatibility. The cocycle cancels the source and composite comparison factors; naturality moves the middle comparison past the source exchange.

Transport the exact pullbacks to left-derived pullbacks by their canonical comparison isomorphisms. The proper mate transport and inverse open exchange transport identify exactly rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap. Cancel the pullback comparison isomorphisms to obtain the required equality. Reuse the proved exact_exchange_transport helper from UnboundedEtaleCompactSupportComparisons; its statement has no Noetherian or quasi-compact hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: R9: explicit factorwise proof of the parent graph compositor argument, retaining ordinary unbounded categories and the original hypotheses.

theorem sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso_baseChange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g' : Y' ⟶ Z'}
    {a : X' ⟶ X} {b : Y' ⟶ Y} {c : Z' ⟶ Z}
    [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification (f ≫ g)]
    [HasCompactification f'] [HasCompactification g'] [HasCompactification (f' ≫ g')]
    [QuasiCompact f'] [QuasiCompact g'] [QuasiCompact (f' ≫ g')]
    (sqf : IsPullback a f' f b) (sqg : IsPullback b g' g c)
    (sqh : IsPullback a (f' ≫ g') (f ≫ g) c)
    (M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) :
    L((c)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).map
        ((sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso A f g
          (HasCompactification.compactification f)
          (HasCompactification.compactification g)
          (HasCompactification.compactification (f ≫ g))).hom.app M) ≫
      (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap A sqg).app
        (R(f)_![ModuleCat.{u + 1} A].obj M) ≫
      R(g')_![ModuleCat.{u + 1} A].map
        ((rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap A sqf).app M) =
    (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap A sqh).app M ≫
      (sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso A f' g'
        (HasCompactification.compactification f')
        (HasCompactification.compactification g')
        (HasCompactification.compactification (f' ≫ g'))).hom.app
          (L((a)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).obj M)
